focus: Q2 — integration references: what references/mcp-imagician.md, references/mcp-video-audio.md and assets/hls-video-conversion.md become as files and Knowledge documents, the tool-first rewrite with the ffmpeg fallback, the legacy vocabulary to drop across every referrer, and whether the tools catalogue is a third reference file

label: The server's tool layer is not ffmpeg for images: Image group is sharp-backed (8 tools) while Audio, Video and Media groups are ffmpeg-backed (31 tools), so 'FFmpeg Image Operations' misnames the primary layer for the image route
evidence: mcp server/README.md section 4 groups the 39 tools as Image (sharp) 8, Audio (ffmpeg) 6, Video (ffmpeg) 20, Media 5

label: Measured legacy-vocabulary inventory: live carriers are the 2 skill reference filenames, 2 Knowledge filenames, the plugin skill copy, AGENTS.md (4 lines), sk-media-editor/README.md (5 lines), SKILL.md (6 lines), benchmark/router/README.md (2 lines), benchmark/gates/README.md (4 lines), systems.py (2 keys), the playbook (3 files / 4 lines) and SYNC.md dated notes; INSTALL-GUIDE.md, USER-GUIDE.md, rule_parity.py and the app-level Commands/root AGENTS.md carry zero hits
SYNC.md's dated entries quote the retired server names as history; a legacy-vocabulary pass must exclude dated records and benchmark/reports, or it rewrites the audit trail the system keeps

The router resolves resource names against the live inventory and 'a renamed or deleted reference degrades to a smaller resource set instead of a dead path or crash', so a rename that misses RESOURCE_MAP, the router fixtures or route_contract.py fails silently rather than loudly

The tools catalogue must be a third reference file rather than tables added beside the two: 5 Media-group tools and the media_setup_ffmpeg consent contract are cross-media, so a per-media split would scatter or duplicate them

assets/hls-video-conversion.md needs no rename (its filename and Knowledge title carry no legacy word) but its content is ffmpeg-only while the video_hls_ladder tool exists, so its change is a tool-first rewrite plus a version bump

benchmark/router/README.md publishes an output example with "tool": "video-audio" and a decision rule 'IMAGE binds Imagician, VIDEO/AUDIO bind Video-Audio', so the router contract itself carries the retired tool ids
Both integration references already open with a tool-aware Precondition paragraph but name no tool, so the tool-first rewrite is a body rewrite rather than a new framing

mcp server/claude-plugin/skills/media-editor/ ships its own references/ and assets/ copy plus description.json and graph-metadata.json, so a skill rename reaches generated packaging and those two JSON files are an unverified rename surface

direction: Absorb the tool tables into the two media-type references and ship no third document
reason: The Media group (media_health, media_probe, media_repair, media_remove_silence, media_setup_ffmpeg) is cross-media and the consent contract and error codes are cross-cutting; a per-media split scatters or duplicates them, and the server's own README already carries one grouped catalogue as the single source

direction: Rename only the filenames and leave the bodies ffmpeg-first
reason: The image group is sharp-backed, so an ffmpeg-first body under a corrected name still misdescribes the primary route and leaves the tool layer unnamed at the point of use

direction: Sweep the legacy vocabulary repo-wide including dated change records and benchmark reports
reason: SYNC.md entries and benchmark reports are dated records of decisions already taken; rewriting them destroys the audit trail and the system's own rule that a dated entry is a record, not a description of the present
